options: The V8 JavaScript engine (the same one Chrome uses) running as a standalone program outside the browser, with extra APIs browsers don't provide
A separate programming language unrelated to JavaScript
A web browser designed for developers
A cloud hosting service for websites
questions.explain: Node.js embeds the V8 engine in a standalone runtime, giving JavaScript access to things a browser withholds for security, like direct file system and raw network access.

questions.q: Why can't a browser-based web page do the same things a Node.js blockchain script can (e.g. read a private key from an environment variable)?
options: Browsers intentionally restrict file system, raw network, and environment-variable access for security reasons
Browsers don't support the ethers or viem libraries at all
JavaScript in a browser cannot use bigint
Private keys only exist in Node.js, never in any form in a browser
questions.explain: Browsers deliberately sandbox pages away from the file system, raw sockets, and arbitrary process/environment access — Node removes that sandbox since it runs as a trusted local or server program.

questions.q: What does running `node` with no file argument do?
options: It prints the installed npm version only
It immediately exits with an error
It opens the REPL, an interactive prompt for evaluating JavaScript one line at a time
It starts an Express server automatically
questions.explain: The REPL (Read-Eval-Print Loop) lets you type and evaluate JavaScript expressions interactively, useful for quickly testing a line of syntax.

questions.q: What decides whether a Node.js file uses CommonJS (require) or ES modules (import)?
options: The project's package.json "type" field (or a .mjs/.cjs file extension), not a global Node setting
The version of npm installed
Whether the file is inside a 'src' folder
CommonJS and ES modules can always be freely mixed in the same file
questions.explain: package.json's "type": "module" switches a project to ESM; "type": "commonjs" (or omitting it) keeps CommonJS; .mjs/.cjs extensions override that per file.

questions.q: Which of these is a Node.js API that a plain browser script does NOT have access to?
options: The `fs` module for reading and writing files on disk
The `fetch` function for making network requests
Arithmetic operators like + and -
Variables declared with `const`
questions.explain: fetch and basic JavaScript syntax exist in browsers too; direct file system access via `fs` is one of the capabilities Node adds that a browser sandbox deliberately withholds.
